A startup should do things that don't scale at the very beginning, because that is how the first users are won over by hand, one at a time, with real effort.

The most common unscalable thing founders have to do at the start is to recruit users manually, which sounds unglamorous but works better than almost anything else.

Nearly all startups have to. You can't wait for users to come to you, so you go out and get them yourself, one by one, until word of mouth takes over.
